App blocking, local foreground usage measurement, shared Hybrid allowance accounting, optional UsageStats reconciliation, optional on-device DNS-only website filtering, Android Keystore Accountability PIN protection, and optional 24-hour voluntary removal cooling-off operate offline on-device. Remote category feed updates remain disabled until a signed feed and pinned public key are configured; YouTube Shorts-only detection remains post-MVP.
Detects when a restricted app enters the foreground during an active commitment

MIZAN uses this accessibility service strictly to detect the package name of the foreground app so it can present a blocking screen for apps you chose to restrict during an active commitment. MIZAN never reads screen text, captures screenshots, logs keystrokes, or uploads data off your device.
Android Accessibility Service is enabled and connected. Restricted apps are evaluated against your local commitment rules in real time.
MIZAN accessibility permission is enabled, but the system service is currently disconnected or interrupted. Open Accessibility Settings or check battery optimization to restore enforcement.
MIZAN cannot automatically grant accessibility access. Enable Mizan App Restriction Monitor in Android Accessibility Settings to enforce selected app restrictions.
MIZAN could not verify system accessibility status or local rule state. Enforcement fails safely without blocking apps until state recovers.
Privacy promise: MIZAN observes only foreground package transitions. It never reads window text, messages, passwords, or screenshots, and sends zero data off-device.
Unable to open Android Accessibility Settings on this device.
Android Usage Access is enabled. MIZAN can run local, deduplicated interval reconciliation using foreground and background timestamps for your selected restricted apps.

Optional permission: granting Usage Access in Android Settings allows MIZAN to reconcile closed historical intervals for selected restricted apps after process restarts. While disabled, historical totals are not verified as complete.
MIZAN could not verify Android Usage Access status or history on this device. Usage measurement falls back safely without assuming missing totals are complete.
On-device guarantee: MIZAN reads only package names and foreground/background event timestamps for your commitment window. Unrelated apps are excluded, and no usage data leaves your device.

Local DNS filtering tunnel is established on 10.120.0.1/32 (DNS queries only). Allowed queries are forwarded via your active network DNS resolvers; no MIZAN server is used.
Local DNS filtering was stopped by you. MIZAN will not silently restart it without your action.

Another VPN is currently active on this device. Android permits only one active VPN at a time, so MIZAN DNS filtering is inactive.
Local DNS filtering encountered an error and stopped safely. App restriction enforcement and usage measurement remain active.

• MIZAN uses Android VPN permission strictly for local on-device DNS filtering.
• Android allows only one active VPN at a time; enabling MIZAN may displace another VPN.
• Filtering is domain-based only — not HTTPS URL-path or page-content filtering.
• Encrypted DNS (Private DNS / DoH), hard-coded IPs, proxies, and other bypasses can circumvent DNS filtering.
• Ordinary browsing traffic is NOT routed through a remote MIZAN server.
• Shared domains (such as shared CDNs) can cause legitimate services to become inaccessible.
I understand how MIZAN local DNS filtering works and its limitations.
Warning: Android Private DNS (encrypted DNS-over-TLS) appears active on your network. Encrypted DNS bypasses local UDP port-53 VPN DNS filtering unless disabled in Android Network settings.

Mode: Strict — selected apps remain paused for the duration of your 7-day commitment.

Pause intentionally. Take a breath, return to your home screen, or open MIZAN to review your commitment.
MIZAN helps you set voluntary, calm boundaries on your own terms — without feeds, guilt, accounts, or tracking.
Commitments begin as configurable drafts and remain inactive until you review every rule and deliberately agree. At the end of 7 days, nothing auto-renews — you decide your next step.
Your commitments, rules, and preferences stay strictly on this device. MIZAN includes zero cloud sync, zero analytics, and zero advertisements.

To detect restricted apps entering the foreground and measure foreground usage, Android requires you to manually enable MIZAN in Accessibility Settings. You can also optionally grant Usage Access to reconcile historical usage intervals locally, and optionally grant local VPN permission if you choose DNS-based website filtering. MIZAN never reads screen text, typed input, or screenshots, and never stores or uploads DNS query history.

Filter exact domains and their subdomains (e.g., example.com blocks example.com and sub.example.com without affecting notexample.com). Filtering is domain-only and best-effort via a local Android VPN interface.
Require Accountability PIN for emergency termination
A local salted PBKDF2 PIN (protected by Android Keystore) is configured. Enabling this adds intentional friction before ending an active commitment early.
No Accountability PIN is configured yet. Configure one in Settings before enabling PIN protection on this commitment.
Local PIN protection is a voluntary accountability deterrent; it cannot prevent OS uninstall, force-stop, safe mode, ADB, or factory reset.
Carefully confirm every rule below before activating your 7-day commitment.
7 full days (168 hours from activation). Does not auto-renew at completion. Allowance and rules lock once activated.

App blocking and foreground usage measurement depend on Android Accessibility Settings (and optional Usage Access) and OEM background behavior. If website filtering is enabled, local DNS filtering requires user-consented Android VPN authorization, covers DNS domains only (not URL paths, content, Private DNS, proxies, or hard-coded IPs), and respects Android\'s one-active-VPN limit.

End an active commitment immediately before its 7-day period completes.
Your commitment will end immediately and be recorded locally as Emergency Terminated — separate from a normal 7-day completion. Rules will no longer apply.

Accountability PIN protection is required for this commitment, but the local Keystore-backed PIN credential could not be verified. Emergency termination remains locked until either the PIN credential recovers or a 24-hour voluntary removal request in Settings finishes.
Enter your 4–8 digit Accountability PIN to authorize early emergency termination.

I understand this will immediately end my active commitment early and record an emergency termination.
Local preferences, privacy guarantees, and enforcement service health.

A trusted partner or your own future self can configure a local 4–8 digit PIN. MIZAN stores only a salted PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 hash sealed with Android Keystore (AES-256-GCM) in no-backup storage. This is a voluntary deterrent, not tamper-proof device administration.
Start a calm 24-hour cooling-off timer before lifting commitment restrictions or clearing an Accountability PIN locally. You can cancel anytime, or complete deactivation once 24 hours have elapsed.
Honest limitation: This cooling-off period is a voluntary deterrent. Android never allows an ordinary app to block OS uninstall, force-stop, safe mode, ADB, or factory reset.
Update local filter datasets on Wi-Fi only
Remote category dataset updates remain disabled because no signed external feed and pinned public verification key are configured. Custom blocked and allowlisted domains work 100% offline.

MIZAN stores all commitments, rules, and preferences exclusively in local Room and DataStore storage (excluded from cloud backup). MIZAN never stores DNS query history or browsing logs, and includes zero accounts, cloud sync, analytics, ads, or remote servers.

App restriction and live foreground timing require manual Accessibility Service opt-in. Optional Usage Access enables local interval reconciliation, and optional local VPN authorization enables on-device DNS domain filtering.
MIZAN is exempt from aggressive system battery throttling, helping Accessibility and local VPN enforcement remain stable across idle periods.
Android battery optimization is active for MIZAN. Some devices may pause Accessibility or local VPN monitoring in the background.
